items.title: SEVP issues BCM 2611-03 on the November 17 CPT stay and injunction
items.summary: On 20 November 2026 SEVP issued Broadcast Message 2611-03, ‘Preliminary Injunction and Stay Issued on Curricular Practical Training Broadcast Messages Disseminated on August 12, 2026, and August 24, 2026,’ to all SEVIS users. The message reports the 17 November 2026 D. Mass. preliminary injunction and stay in Association of American Universities v. DHS, No. 1:26-cv-14520, and quotes the party-specific Rule 65 injunction from ECF 36 p. 24 (defendants enjoined from carrying out the August 12 and August 24 interpretation of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(f)(10)(i) as to the plaintiffs and each of their members, including employees and students, prospectively and as to pre-broadcast conduct and approvals). ICE has also added banner text on the SEVIS What's New and SEVIS home pages that the August 12 (BCM 2608-01) and August 24 (BCM 2608-02) broadcasts ‘are enjoined and stayed and should not be relied on or followed at this time.’ The underlying court posture is unchanged: ECF 36 remains operative, including the nationwide APA § 705 stay (broadcasts may not be enforced or applied pending judicial review) that BCM 2611-03 does not quote. No notice of appeal or stay pending appeal was found (last known filing still 17 November 2026; CourtListener last updated 22 November 2026, 6:08 a.m.). Study in the States is not yet updated. Already-denied CPT is not automatically restored; the BCM adds no rescission instruction. DSO authorization still applies. This remains preliminary relief, not a final judgment. Not legal advice.
items.slate_impact: Material for the entire Fall 2027 CS/MBA/MSF international slate, especially internship-heavy paths. Official SEVP guidance to all SEVIS users now reflects the 17 November stay and injunction; the August broadcasts had treated elective for-credit internships, co-ops, and practicums as ineligible for CPT. Call out MSF separately: many MSF/MFE/quant internships are elective or for-credit rather than required of every student in the degree. This is agency notice of existing preliminary relief, not a new substantive CPT rule and not automatic restoration of already-denied CPT. DSO authorization still applies. Subject to appeal. Study in the States is not yet updated. Not school-specific as a new ISSS policy.
